# Open issues (beta)

Tessero 0.2.0 is in beta; this open-issues list is at revision **v3** (it is bumped as
issues are resolved). It is the tracked list of what stands between the beta and a stable release, ranked by
priority. The same list is imported into GitHub Issues with `php tools/beta-issues.php create`; after the
import, GitHub is the source of truth and this page is a snapshot from 2026-09-28.

| Priority | Issues |
|---|---:|
| P0 | 12 |
| P1 | 19 |
| P2 | 9 |
| P3 | 13 |
| **Total open** | **53** |
| Resolved | 2 |

The feature items (P3) come from the [NumPy/SciPy gap analysis](numpy-scipy-gap-analysis.md). The steps for testing outside the
Linux review host are in the [live-testing checklist](../operations/live-testing.md).

## Details

### TSR-001

**Run the CI matrix for the first time** (P0; ci, beta-exit)

ci.yml and nightly.yml have never executed. Every result so far comes from one Linux x86-64 host with PHP 8.4.

Acceptance criteria:

- ci.yml green on push for PHP 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 (NTS and ZTS) on ubuntu-latest
- Kernel ASan/UBSan, extension phpt, FFI PHPUnit (JIT off/function/tracing), fuzz smoke and docs build jobs all pass
- nightly.yml completes one full run (5.5 h soak per backend, 30 min fuzz per target)
- Failures triaged into issues

### TSR-002

**Windows: build and test kernel, extension and FFI package** (P0; platform:windows, beta-exit)

The Win32 paths in csrc/src/mmap.c (CreateFileMapping/MapViewOfFile) and the C11 atomics in alloc.c have never been compiled. The extension must build with the PHP SDK (MSVC); the kernel DLL with MSVC or MinGW.

Acceptance criteria:

- libtessero.dll builds; the C suite passes (270 checks)
- php_tessero.dll builds with the PHP SDK for 8.3/8.4 NTS and TS; phpt passes
- FFI suite passes against the DLL, including memmap modes r, r+, w+, c
- MemorySafetyTest and BackendParityTest pass
- Windows job added to ci.yml

### TSR-003

**macOS arm64 and x86_64 builds** (P0; platform:macos, beta-exit)

Apple clang has no OpenMP by default, Accelerate or OpenBLAS must be found for LAPACK, and the NEON paths in vmath.h and sort.c are untested.

Acceptance criteria:

- Kernel builds with and without libomp (Homebrew)
- The C suite and FFI suite pass on arm64 (M-series) and x86_64
- Extension builds via phpize; phpt passes
- exp/log accuracy test (< 1 ulp) passes on NEON
- macOS jobs in ci.yml

### TSR-004

**Linux arm64 and Alpine/musl builds** (P0; platform:linux, beta-exit)

Docker images and Graviton servers are common deployment targets. musl differs in libm accuracy, dlopen and the default thread stack size.

Acceptance criteria:

- All suites pass on ubuntu-24.04-arm
- All suites pass in php:8.3-cli-alpine and php:8.4-fpm-alpine
- The Dockerfile example in the docs builds on both architectures

### TSR-005

**Live Laravel application testing** (P0; laravel, beta-exit)

The bridge is covered by package tests only. It needs a real application: Laravel 10/11/12, database casts, queued jobs, Horizon, Octane (Swoole, RoadRunner, FrankenPHP).

Acceptance criteria:

- Sample app: casts round-trip through MySQL/PostgreSQL/SQLite
- Jobs that allocate arrays run 10 000 times under Horizon with memory_in_use back at baseline
- Octane with each server: settings (threads, budget) reset per request and never leak between requests
- tools/soak.php workload called from a route under load (wrk/k6) for 1 h with no growth
- Findings recorded in docs/laravel

### TSR-006

**PHP-FPM with opcache preload under real traffic** (P0; deployment, beta-exit)

tests/e2e/preload.sh checks one CLI start. Real FPM pools with pm=dynamic, reloads and several pools sharing one preload are untested.

Acceptance criteria:

- FPM with opcache.preload=resources/preload.php and ffi.enable=preload serves 1M requests without error
- A graceful reload (kill -USR2) keeps working; no temp header files left behind
- A bad TESSERO_LIB fails at start with the version-check message

### TSR-007

**24-72 hour soak runs on both backends** (P0; reliability, beta-exit)

Only 30 minutes per backend have been run. The release checklist requires 24 h per backend and 72 h before 1.0.

Acceptance criteria:

- php tools/soak.php --backend=ffi --duration=86400 --log=... reports PASS
- Same for --backend=ext
- JSONL logs attached to the release; RSS slope under 64 KiB/min

### TSR-008

**Coverage-guided fuzzing with libFuzzer** (P0; security, reliability, beta-exit)

The review environment could only run the standalone mutation driver (about 13M inputs). Real libFuzzer with coverage feedback has not run.

Acceptance criteria:

- make -C csrc fuzz builds with clang -fsanitize=fuzzer,address,undefined
- Each target (slice, npy, mmap_plan, json) runs 8 h with no crash
- New corpus entries committed; the nightly job keeps running

### TSR-009

**ZTS / FrankenPHP: thread safety of process-wide settings** (P0; concurrency, beta-exit)

Thread count, memory budget and error state are process-wide in the kernel. Under ZTS (FrankenPHP worker mode, parallel extension) two PHP threads can change them concurrently.

Acceptance criteria:

- Document which settings are process-wide and which are per-thread
- Budget accounting is atomic under concurrent allocation (TSan run clean)
- FrankenPHP worker mode test with 8 threads for 1 h: no data race reports, settings behave as documented

### TSR-010

**Independent code and security review of csrc/ and ext/** (P0; security, beta-exit)

One author so far. The memory-safety review (F-1 to F-9) was an internal audit.

Acceptance criteria:

- A reviewer with C and Zend API experience signs off on csrc/ and ext/
- Findings are filed as issues and fixed or accepted with a rationale
- The security policy lists a private reporting contact

### TSR-011

**Publish on Packagist and PIE** (P0; release, beta-exit)

composer require and pie install work only from registered packages. tessero/laravel and tessero/tessero-ext need subtree splits.

Acceptance criteria:

- tessero/tessero, tessero/laravel and tessero/tessero-ext on Packagist
- pie install tessero/tessero-ext works on Linux and macOS
- Install instructions in the docs verified from a clean machine

### TSR-108

**Cross-CPU last-bit determinism** (P1; numerics)

target_clones and compiler FMA contraction can change the last bit between CPUs (AVX2, AVX-512, NEON). Reductions and exp/log must produce the documented results everywhere. The reference side is settled by ADR 0012: fixtures are generated with NumPy's AVX-512 dispatch disabled, so the reference equals the C library's results on every CPU.

Acceptance criteria:

- Decide and document the policy: bit-identical across ISAs, or within 1 ulp
- -ffp-contract setting pinned in the build
- A fixture test run on AVX2, AVX-512 and NEON in CI

### TSR-109

**Port NumPy's indexing and broadcasting tests** (P1; testing)

Our slicing tests are our own. NumPy's test_indexing.py and test_numeric broadcasting cases would catch edge cases we have not thought of.

Acceptance criteria:

- The applicable cases are translated into PHPUnit data providers
- They run on both backends
- Differences are fixed or documented

### TSR-116

**scipy.special: the non-ufunc functions and complex-valued functions** (P3; feature, scipy)

All real-valued scipy.special ufuncs are implemented from SciPy's own code. Missing: the Python-level functions (comb, perm, factorial*, zeta, polygamma, spherical_*, logsumexp, softmax, the *_zeros and roots_* families, lqn/lqmn, ...) and complex-valued functions (hankel*, kelvin, wofz, sph_harm_y), which need complex operands in the kernel function registry.

Acceptance criteria:

### TSR-118

**BLOCKED: barnard_exact and boschloo_exact need scipy.optimize.shgo** (P3; feature, scipy, blocked)

Both tests maximise the p-value over the nuisance parameter with SciPy's shgo; matching SciPy's result needs shgo's exact sampling and local-minimisation sequence.

Acceptance criteria:

- shgo (simplicial, default options) matching SciPy's iterates
- Both tests verified by SciPy fixtures on both backends

### TSR-119

**Integer comparisons above 2^53 in argpartition and nanargmin/nanargmax** (P2; numerics)

ptp, the nan-reductions, cumulative sums and products, partition and correlate/convolve now compute integer inputs in int64 with NumPy's wrap-around (CORE_INT64). argpartition and nanargmin/nanargmax still compare int64 values as float64, so values that differ only above 2^53 can tie.

Acceptance criteria:

- int64 comparisons for integer inputs
- Fixtures with values above 2^53

### TSR-120

**Bound the work of untrusted size arguments** (P2; security, reliability)

Where SciPy's algorithm is slow for huge arguments, Tessero runs the same algorithm: orthogonal polynomials with n around 1e9 loop n times, and anderson_ksamp, siegelslopes and percentileofscore are quadratic in the sample size. SciPy behaves the same, but a PHP web worker fed untrusted sizes can be tied up. Memory is already bounded: allocations sized by a parameter respect the budget, and RAM when no budget is set.

Acceptance criteria:

- A per-call work budget (tessero.max_work or similar) that raises instead of running unbounded loops
- Documented in the operations manual

### TSR-121

**Coverage inventory understates real coverage (shipped facade classes and Np methods untracked)** (P1; bug, parity, docs, generated)

The generated coverage page (docs/project/numpy-scipy-coverage.md, rendered live at the website /docs/coverage) reports about 60% FFI and 43% extension, far below real coverage. Two causes. First, tools/api-dump.php's class list omits five shipped FFI facade classes (ScipyLinalg, Distance, Signal, Ndimage, Csgraph), so they never reach api.json and their areas read 0%. Second, tools/gap_inventory.py's curated rows leave many shipped functions with empty references (Np vstack/split/tile/pad/outer/einsum/polyfit/interp/gradient/trapezoid/logspace/diag and more, Special logsumexp/polygamma/comb/factorial, Integrate Quad::quad, Spatial KDTree::query, Datetime), which render as not-available. No gate step verifies that the inventory references every shipped class: the generator only catches references to functions that do not exist, never shipped functions that have no reference, so the page drifts silently.

Acceptance criteria:

- api-dump.php dumps every generated facade class (ScipyLinalg, Distance, Signal, Ndimage, Csgraph)
- gap_inventory.py rows and aliases reference all shipped functions; coverage.md regenerated
- A gate check fails if any shipped facade class or public registry function is unreferenced by the inventory
- The website /docs/coverage shows the corrected numbers

### TSR-207

**Re-baseline the pinned fixture environment from SkylakeX (AVX-512) to Haswell (AVX2)** (P2; process, numerics, ci)

The pinned reference environment (ADR 0012) forced OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=SkylakeX, an AVX-512 OpenBLAS kernel that is an illegal instruction on AVX2 hosts. The canonical fixture host is AVX2, so fixtures could not be regenerated there and adding any new function was blocked. Re-baselined to the Haswell OpenBLAS kernel, which runs on any AVX2+ CPU; single-threaded BLAS (OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1) keeps the summation order deterministic. Transcendental fixtures also shift about 1 ulp from the old host because of glibc/libm version differences, within the test tolerances.

Acceptance criteria:

- fixture_env.py and gen-fixtures.sh pin OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell; ADR 0012 updated
- All fixtures regenerated on the canonical AVX2 host; full gate green on both backends
- Fixture generation documented to require an AVX2+ host

### TSR-314

**NumPy/SciPy gap-closure roadmap (tiered register with algorithms and PHP-ecosystem analysis)** (P3; feature, parity, numpy, scipy)

docs/project/numpy-scipy-gap-register.md enumerates every genuine remaining gap with the implementation algorithm, a portability verdict (including NumPy dtype/idiom features that do not map to a PHP numeric API), and whether the PHP ecosystem already covers it. Research finding: PHP has no implementation anywhere for all of scipy.signal, ODE solvers (solve_ivp/odeint), computational geometry (ConvexHull/Delaunay/Voronoi), scipy.ndimage array filters, the entire sparse ecosystem (formats, direct and iterative solvers, sparse eigensolvers), matrix functions (expm/logm/sqrtm), nonlinear and global optimization, Schur/QZ, NNLS, and N-D FFT. Tiers: 1 compose from shipped primitives; 2 real algorithm, no new dependency; 3 external C library (QHull/ARPACK/SuiteSparse/HiGHS) or heavy native; 4 not applicable to PHP. heaviside landed as the first Tier-1 item.

Acceptance criteria:

- Tier-1 batch implemented and verified on both backends (nd-FFT, ufunc fills, multivariate randoms, softmax/log_softmax/perm, simpson/cumulative_trapezoid, minimize_scalar, sparse diags, Polynomial)
- Tier-2 and Tier-3 items tracked as sub-issues
- The coverage page reflects each capability as it lands
